status: Source-derived benchmark operationalization; not expert gold or scientific necessity certification.

interpretation.evidence: quote is the published factual statement; requirement_judgment is the separate benchmark inclusion judgment; criterion describes candidate-explicit evidence without assuming published values.
interpretation.selector_matching: NAME matches exact named entities, normalizing typographic hyphens only. ROLE is route-local. execution_context limits phase applicability and is part of matching, not just commentary.
interpretation.scope: ROUTE preparation rows count once per (route identity, requirement id), even when multiple selectors or repeated baths match. The nine named MACS recipe requirements remain nine distinct obligations. OPERATION rows count per distinct applicable operation; sample decalcification is its own conditional pretreatment, not repeated over clearing baths.
interpretation.deduplication: Do not count the same operation/dimension/subject obligation twice through NAME and ROLE matches. Grouped preparation rows are one composite obligation, not additional hidden denominator slots.
interpretation.applicability: Only REQUIRED_PROCEDURE_SPECIFICATION belongs to the unconditional denominator. CONDITIONAL activates only for the quoted condition in its execution context. OPTIONAL never inflates the required denominator.
interpretation.uncertainty: No supplementary material or external facts were used. Approximate durations, alternative repetition counts, and tissue dependence remain as stated; the contract does not certify scientific sufficiency.
interpretation.value_evaluation: Criteria test explicit executable specification and linkage. Any assessment of conformity with a published value must use the cited quote as evidence, never impute that value into missing candidate text. Explicitness/completeness is not the same as agreement with published values. Keep conformity judgments separate.
interpretation.phase_scope: Each phase_scope is a nonempty array whose members are DEHYDRATION, RI_MATCHING, CLEARING, STORAGE, or PREPARATION. Matching requires source route, selector eligibility, phase membership, applicability, and execution_context together. A name alone never overrides phase. Initial DBE concentration applies only to RI_MATCHING, never STORAGE or restoration merely because DBE occurs there.
interpretation.preparation_matching: For PREPARATION rows, NAME selectors identify the prepared recipe/reagent and ROLE selectors identify the owning route process. Evaluate route-level preparation evidence rather than requiring the same preparation to be restated at each bath. Phase is not inferred from dimension: optional terminal heating and restoration have dimension preparation but CLEARING phase; conditional decalcification is a PREPARATION operation.
interpretation.evidence_boundary: A quoted source passage in candidate material remains source evidence unless candidate-authored executable instructions explicitly adopt and link it to the candidate operation or named recipe. Citation, quotation, or matching source wording alone must never supply an inferred candidate value.

Assess conformity separately; alternative suppliers or products are not automatically non-explicit.
requirements.requirement_judgment: Include once per downstream route as a composite preparation/procurement explicitness obligation because the source explicitly calls high-quality organic solvents critical for clearing. Requiring an actionable selection is a benchmark operationalization, not a source-defined numerical purity standard or scientific necessity certification.
requirements.execution_context: Preparation/procurement of organic solvents used in downstream clearing; count once per route, not once per selector, solvent, or bath. Excludes upstream staining buffers and imaging equipment.
requirements.source_uncertainty: Very high quality is qualitative. The source gives product examples in the separate reagents passage and permits carefully considered substitutions, but defines no universal purity percentage, oxidation assay, acceptance threshold, or preparation treatment. None may be invented or required as published facts.

excluded_notes.quote:
Light sheet microscope
The use of a light sheet microscope (e.g. LaVision Biotec.) is recommended. The sample
is ready to be directly imaged in the microscope chamber filled with DBE. Light sheet
allows fast imaging of a large field of view, with very deep optical penetration and
limited photobleaching.
excluded_notes.why: Imaging equipment recommendation outside downstream clearing operation comparison.

excluded_notes.quote:
Scanning microscope (confocal or 2-photon)
Upright confocal and 2-photon microscopes can image the sample with a depth up to
the working distance of the objective at high resolution. A chamber has to be built to
confine the DBE and protect the microscope. To build an imaging chamber:
1. The chamber (Script provided at iDISCO.info) can be 3D printed with Visijet M3
Crystal resin, which is resistant to DBE.
2. Secure the chamber to the microscope slide with Kwik-sil epoxy (VWR). This epoxy
does not permanently bond so that sample and spacers can be recovered after
imaging. Make sure there are no gaps that the DBE can leak through.
3. Place a drop of epoxy in the center of the chamber and place sample on drop.
4. Close the chamber by gluing a coverslip to the spacer with the epoxy. Do not glue
over filling inlet.
5. Fill the chamber with DBE with a pipet through the filling inlet.
6. Plug the inlet with epoxy.
excluded_notes.why: Conditional imaging branch outside downstream clearing operation comparison.
